slides.title: AVCC: Audio-Visual Conversation Corpus for Turn-Taking Prediction with a Human Benchmark
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a public benchmark for multiparty next-speaker prediction using single-camera and microphone setups, directly addressing the sensor constraints relevant to HyECHO's goal of observing hybrid human-AI team states.

card.one_liner: AVCC establishes a public audio-visual benchmark for multiparty turn-taking prediction with a human performance reference.
card.key_idea: Converts 31-hour single-camera/mic corpus into NSP benchmark with speaker-disjoint test partition, transcripts, and human baseline.
card.evaluation: Scored RoleVAP and MuVAP on 1,730 events against 154 human participants using balanced accuracy for hold/shift and next-speaker tasks.
card.limitation: Human participants lacked access to cues within the silence gap, potentially underestimating visual signals available to models.

slides.title: Dyship: Leveraging Acoustic Features For Speaker Relationship Classification From Dyadic Conversations
slides.highlight: The study demonstrates that conventional acoustic features and self-supervised speech representations can effectively classify speaker familiarity and kinship in dyadic conversations, offering a non-data-hungry approach to inferring social relationships from audio.

card.one_liner: Acoustic features outperform LLMs in classifying speaker familiarity and kinship from dyadic conversations.
card.key_idea: Compares five speech representations (spectral, SSLR, x-vectors, articulatory) using ResNet/SVM classifiers with utterance-level aggregation.
card.evaluation: Tested on Seamless Interaction corpus; spectral features best for familiarity, WavLM/x-vectors for kinship, exceeding human/LLM baselines.
card.limitation: Limited to one dataset with few test dyads; lacks explicit modeling of turn-taking or cross-speaker temporal dynamics.

slides.title: Robots That Talk Too Much and Don't Listen Enough
slides.highlight: The paper argues that multimodal bidirectional streaming is essential to reduce turn-taking failures in social robot interactions, addressing a key challenge for robust human-AI team state observation.

card.one_liner: Multimodal bidirectional streaming reduces turn-taking failures in social robot interactions.
card.key_idea: Enabling robots to listen and observe while speaking via bidirectional audio/video streaming to detect interruptions and user distress.
card.evaluation: Qualitative analysis of 2012/2025 robot dialogues and experiments with Google ADK for object recognition and barge-in handling.
card.limitation: Lacks quantitative metrics; relies on specific APIs (Google ADK, Furhat) and anecdotal evidence rather than controlled user studies.

slides.title: Teamknitt: Configuring, Observing and Intervening in LLM-Agent Teams through the Lens of Dynamical-Systems and Human-Team Theory
slides.highlight: This paper introduces a framework for observing and intervening in LLM-agent teams using human-team theory, offering methods for tracking distributed coordination and emergent states that align with HyECHO's goal of modeling hybrid human-AI team dynamics.

card.one_liner: Teamknitt applies human-team theory to configure, observe, and intervene in LLM agent teams via explicit topologies.
card.key_idea: Framework offering 14 routing topologies, sharing profiles, and bounded interventions, separating member attributes from interaction dynamics.
card.evaluation: System description with reference implementation; no comparative results reported, only falsifiable hypotheses and offline demonstrations.
card.limitation: Human-team theory transfer to AI is unverified; emergent states like trust are declared unmeasured rather than inferred.

slides.title: Kezek: Splitting Mono Two-Person Conversations into Per-Speaker Tracks for Full-Duplex Dialogue Data
slides.highlight: Kezek separates mono two-person conversations into per-speaker tracks, preserving overlaps and short backchannels, which supports HyECHO's goal of modeling hybrid human-AI team states like engagement and turn-taking.

card.one_liner: Kezek splits mono two-person audio into per-speaker tracks, preserving short replies and timing for full-duplex dialogue training.
card.key_idea: Two-stage pipeline: global speaker identification via phase-insensitive fingerprint, followed by conditioned time-domain separation with strict mixture consistency.
card.evaluation: Compared against pyannote-DialogueSidon on Open Yap and CallHome; measures reply retention, leakage, swaps, and speed; shows 4-5x faster inference.
card.limitation: Struggles with quiet replies under louder voices; limited to exactly two speakers; primarily trained and evaluated on English data.

slides.title: Xinhua Unveils Humanoid Robots Designed to Present News
slides.highlight: Xinhua has introduced humanoid robots specifically designed for news presentation, representing a practical application of embodied agents in media and public communication.

slides.title: China unveils world's first bionic humanoid robot news anchors
slides.highlight: The introduction of bionic humanoid robots as news anchors highlights advancements in embodied social presence and human-robot interaction, relevant to the development of socially engaging AI agents.

slides.title: Off-target posterior mass: A training-free diagnostic for fine-tuning spoken language diarization probes
slides.highlight: This paper introduces Off-target Posterior Mass (OTPM), a training-free metric to predict performance gains in Spoken Language Diarization fine-tuning, which is relevant to HyECHO's goal of efficient, non-data-hungry multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: OTPM predicts spoken language diarization fine-tuning gains using unlabelled audio.
card.key_idea: Measures posterior mass assigned to non-target languages in pre-trained LID models to forecast probe gains without training or labels.
card.evaluation: Validated on synthetic FLEURS (Spearman 0.56) and real corpora (SEAME, VoxPopuli, DISPLACE) using Whisper models and LDER metrics.
card.limitation: Weak generalization to real-world data due to synthetic-to-real distribution shifts and failure to model target-language confusion.

slides.title: CFGComposer: Compositional Audio-Text-to-Motion Generation via Copula Score Correction
slides.highlight: This paper addresses the generation of whole-body gestures synchronized with speech and aligned with text, a key capability for embodied social robots. It demonstrates direct sim-to-real transfer on a humanoid robot, which is relevant to the development of natural human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: Composes audio and text diffusion experts via copula score correction for synchronized, semantic gesture generation.
card.key_idea: Derives exact score decomposition to identify omitted cross-modal interaction, then estimates it via a jointly-trained residual model applied as CFG guidance.
card.evaluation: Tested on BEAT dataset; outperforms baselines in semantic fidelity and beat alignment, validated by human studies and Unitree G1 robot deployment.
card.limitation: Requires training a separate joint model on scarce annotated data and incurs extra inference cost for the correction pass.

slides.title: An LLM Is All You Need: Data-Efficient Adaptation to Full-Duplex, Word-Level Spoken Dialogue
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates that a frozen multimodal LLM can be adapted for word-level full-duplex dialogue with minimal data, offering a non-data-hungry approach to modeling turn-taking and backchanneling relevant to HyECHO's goals.

card.one_liner: Adapts a frozen LLM into a full-duplex dialogue system using lightweight adapters and word-level turn-taking tokens.
card.key_idea: A thinker-talker cascade where a frozen LLM emits text and timing tokens per 80ms frame, guided by a finite-state machine for legal turn-taking.
card.evaluation: Tested on Full-Duplex-Bench and InteractionBench; competitive with large-scale systems in backchanneling, interruption handling, and task accuracy.
card.limitation: Requires strict real-time processing within 80ms per frame; talker currently ignores user audio for voice conditioning.

slides.title: Do Large Language Models Show Racial and Sex Bias in Pain Management? A Counterfactual Audit of GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek and Qwen
slides.highlight: This counterfactual audit of major LLMs reveals that model instability and configuration differences outweigh detected racial or sex biases in pain management, highlighting the need for rigorous noise-floor reporting in AI fairness assessments.

card.one_liner: Current LLMs show no detectable racial or sex bias in pain management when accounting for model instability.
card.key_idea: Counterfactual audit of 17 LLMs using paired comparisons on identical seeds, measuring bias against re-sampling noise floors.
card.evaluation: Tested 24 configurations on acute-pain vignettes and Q-Pain cases; no differences survived false discovery rate correction.
card.limitation: Opioid decision bounds were wide, and results may not generalize to all clinical contexts or future model versions.

slides.title: HEIR: Harness Egocentric Intent for Human-Robot Interactions
slides.highlight: HEIR provides a dataset pairing egocentric video, gaze, and speech with robot trajectories to study intent grounding and long-horizon navigation-manipulation tasks, offering relevant resources for embodied social robot interaction research.

card.one_liner: HEIR is a dataset pairing egocentric human cues with robot trajectories to study long-horizon, user-centric human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Combines human gaze, speech, and egocentric video with robot observations and teleoperated navigation-manipulation trajectories in household settings.
card.evaluation: Benchmarks intent grounding, planning, and execution using offline metrics and real-robot tests; shows human cues improve performance but end-to-end success remains low.
card.limitation: High error accumulation in integrated systems leads to low episode-level success rates (18.52%) despite good component-level performance.

slides.title: CineMME: From Dialogue Grounding to Narrative Reasoning in Multimodal Video Understanding
slides.highlight: CineMME evaluates the ability to bind dialogue to speakers and infer narrative meaning, directly addressing HyECHO's goals of diarization, addressee modeling, and understanding group dynamics in multimodal social perception.

card.one_liner: CineMME benchmarks dialogue-grounded plot understanding, revealing models fail to bind speech to speakers.
card.key_idea: Human-verified benchmark linking temporal dialogue grounding, speaker binding, and narrative reasoning across 975 clips.
card.evaluation: Tested 20 MLLMs on reasoning and 9 omni-modal models on grounding using tIoU, WER, vIoU, and MCQ accuracy.
card.limitation: Limited to short English clips; public sources risk pretraining contamination and copyright issues affect reproducibility.

slides.title: NSDL: Neuro-Symbolic Division of Labor for Multi-Robot Task Planning
slides.highlight: This work demonstrates a neuro-symbolic division of labor for multi-robot task planning, separating perceptual judgments handled by vision-language models from deterministic scheduling by solvers. This approach is relevant to MIMIC's exploration of hybrid human-AI societies, as it provides a scalable framework for coordinating heterogeneous agents through complementary neural and symbolic reasoning.

card.one_liner: NSDL splits multi-robot planning between a trained VLM for state judgment and a solver for structure.
card.key_idea: A trained VLM generates a plan sketch of goals and assignments, which a deterministic solver expands into an executable joint plan.
card.evaluation: Tested on VIKI-L2 and new LOCUS-Bench; outperforms baselines with 97% OOD accuracy, showing solver eliminates structural errors.
card.limitation: Remaining failures stem from misjudged states or unlisted goals, as the solver cannot correct the model's initial semantic errors.
